{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"Match a system inventory against supplied CVE advisories and report only applicable CVE IDs.

Input: JSON with `system_profile` (list of installed products with names and versions) and `advisories` (each with id, description, affected).

Output: exactly {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique supplied IDs; empty array if none.

PRODUCT MATCHING (normalize aggressively):
1. Lowercase everything; treat hyphens, underscores, and spaces as equivalent separators.
2. Strip vendor/organization prefixes (e.g., "jetbrains/teamcity" matches an installed product named "teamcity"; "fujielectric/tellus_lite_v-simulator" matches "Tellus Lite V-Simulator").
3. Match if the advisory product name, after removing the vendor prefix, equals the installed product name; also compare full names and package-manager style names. Ignore letter-case differences (Title Case, camelCase).
4. Advisory descriptions may restate the product name in different casing/format ("Proagent", "Weighbridge Automation Software", "e-Belediye", "Satos Mobile") — use these to confirm or resolve the product match when the affected field's naming style differs from the inventory.
5. Do NOT match different products from the same vendor (e.g., installed "jetbrains-hub" does not match "jetbrains/teamcity"; "jetbrains-intellij-idea" does not match "jetbrains/youtrack").
6. An advisory may list multiple affected products joined by OR (e.g., "nozominetworks/cmc: version < 22.6.2 OR nozominetworks/guardian: version < 22.6.2"). It is applicable if ANY branch matches an installed product and version.

VERSION COMPARISON (numeric, segment-wise):
1. Split versions on dots; compare segments as integers left to right. Pad the shorter version with zeros (e.g., 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1; 9.9 == 9.9.0; 4.0.1.0 == 4.0.1).
2. A plain value like "9" or "1.0" compares numerically against multi-segment bounds: 9 < 20230904 is TRUE; 4.0.1.1 vs "= 4.0.1" is NOT equal (4.0.1.1 > 4.0.1), so it is excluded.
3. Operators: "=" exact equality (after zero-padding); "<" strictly less than; "<=" less than or equal (INCLUSIVE — installed version equal to the bound IS affected); ">=" greater than or equal (inclusive). Range "version >= A and < B" or "from A before B" means A <= installed < B.
4. Prose forms: "versions prior to X", "before X", "< X" all mean strictly less than X (installed version equal to X is NOT affected). "up to and including X", "X and prior versions", "<= X" are inclusive. "from A before B" is the half-open range [A, B).
5. Date-like versions (20230904, 2024.3.52635, 20230114) compare numerically segment-wise like any other version; installed 20230904 with "before 20230904" is excluded, installed 20230914 with "prior to 20230904" is excluded (greater).
6. Bounds from descriptions ("prior to 2023.12.0", "before 23.11.13156.0") must be used exactly as stated; do not alter them.

DECISION PROCEDURE:
For each advisory: (a) determine whether any installed product matches the advisory product (applying normalization rules 1-6 above); if not, skip it. (b) If matched, evaluate every affected-branch version condition against the installed version using the numeric rules; if any branch is satisfied, the CVE is applicable. (c) Include each applicable CVE ID exactly once. Do not include CVEs for products not installed, and do not include CVEs whose version condition excludes the installed version.

CRITICAL: Never drop an applicable CVE because the advisory product name uses a different alias style than the inventory (vendor-stripped, title case, package-manager, underscored). Never include a CVE when the installed version equals a strict "<" bound, exceeds an upper bound, or is below a lower bound — check inclusive vs exclusive bounds carefully, including trailing zero segments (installed X.Y.Z.0 equals bound X.Y.Z; installed X.Y.Z.1 does not). Return only the JSON
